_readme: THE FORGE STORE'S SHOP WINDOW — and this file holds no content, only the two decisions that are the
The window itself (which banner in which slot, which shelf over which source, the institutional pages)
is declared by the mounted dataset's `storefront.json`, exactly like the catalogue is declared by its
`catalog.json`. Copying it in here would make this repository the author of a page the platform's own
example data already describes. See seed/forge.json's `_readme` for the same reasoning about the catalogue.
What IS this instance's own answer is below.
_apps_why: The apps this window needs that a fresh box would not already carry. `shelves`, `reviews`,
`subscriptions` and `banners` itself are installed on this bench already (measured); the entry stays
because a clone of this repository against an empty box needs it, and a block cannot be placed by an app
that is not installed.
★ `banners` IS SAFE TO INSTALL ON A SHARED TENANT AND `recommendations` IS NOT — see `_apps_held`. The
difference is `manifest.contact.hooks`: `banners` declares NONE, so installing it places nothing anywhere
and every tile in this window is a deliberate placement.
★★★ pk33 — `demo-gate` IS HERE, AND THE TENANT-WIDE FAN-OUT IS WHY IT IS WANTED RATHER THAN TOLERATED.
THE DECISION: the gate arrives INSTALLED at the demo's birth, and the demo is the four shops — shoes,
outlet, café, totem — so BOTH stores of this tenant get the gate, which is exactly what
installing it here does: it declares ONE storefront hook (`storefront:gate`) and `seedDefaultPlacements`
writes a row per store. `forge` and `outlet` are both served by the reference vitrine and the checkout we
host, and both images COMPOSE this app (`composition.json` → `instanceApps`), so both can draw it.
⚠️ THIS IS THE ONLY DOOR INTO `forgeco`, AND THAT IS NOT A PREFERENCE. `seed/box.json` REFUSES an `apps`
list on a tenant that declares `dataset: true` (`bin/seed-box.mjs::assertOneOwner`) — the dataset one-shot
owns that gesture there — so the shoe brand's installs have to come from a window seed, and this is it.
⛔ AND UNTIL pk33 NOTHING IN THE BIRTH INSTALLED IT AT ALL. The app's README said "Install the app for the
tenant": a hand gesture somebody had to remember, which on the bench of 11/09 nobody had. The demo served
its front door open for days with every birth green underneath — and it could, because nothing anywhere
verified that the gate APPEARS. Step 14-bis does now, on both sides of the dismissal cookie.

_why: THE FIRST LINE OF THE SHOP IS A PROMISE, AND THE ONLY INTERESTING QUESTION ABOUT IT IS WHETHER THE
KERNEL KEEPS IT. The instruction for this band was one clause long: put up a sentence — «Frete grátis
para compras acima de…» — and ONLY IF a free-shipping promotion actually exists.
⇒ SO THE SENTENCE IS HERE AND THE NUMBER IS NOT. `{floor}` is filled from the promotion itself at seed
time (`seed/vitrine.mjs`, `freeShippingFloor`), and if this store carries no promotion that actually
zeroes the freight, NO BAND IS PLACED. A typed number is a promise with an expiry date nobody wrote
down: the day the promotion moves, the shop keeps advertising the old floor and every test stays green.
⚠️ AND THE NUMBER IS R$ 299, NOT R$ 300, WHICH IS WHY DERIVING IS NOT A FLOURISH. This store carries
TWO active free-shipping promotions with different rules — see `promotions._why_two_freights` below —
and only one of them is free shipping in the sense a shopper means. Anybody writing this sentence by
looking at the admin's list has an even chance of writing the wrong one.
⛔ AND THERE IS NO GUARD CONFIRMING THE SENTENCE AGAINST THE PROMOTIONS, deliberately. It was proposed
and REFUSED, 02/09: "esse guard não faz muito sentido, essa barra não é um campo livre no app?" — it
is. The band is a free-text field of the `banners` app, written by the merchant in Compose; the kernel
does not read marketing copy and must not start. The answer to a sentence that can rot is to DERIVE it,
not to police it.
THE DATASET'S promotions.json IS A PRICING BENCH, NOT A SORTIMENT, and the difference decides which of
its sixteen scenarios a SHOP may carry. Most of them exist in deliberately conflicting PAIRS on one
product — 20% against 10% on the same shoe, an exclusive against a willing one — because what they are
there to prove is which promotion the engine picks and in what order. That is the right content for a
bench somebody drives on purpose. In a shop somebody is being shown, a contradictory price does not read
as 'the promotion engine works', it reads as a broken store.
So the four above are the ones that are honest merchandising on their own: a buy-3-pay-2, an automatic
gift over a threshold, capped free shipping, and a Pix discount. Two of them carry `show_progress`, which
is what puts 'faltam R$ X' in the cart — a capability nobody sees if no promotion has a threshold.
The twelve left out are NAMED, not silently dropped, in `_excluded` below: a demo with no promotion at
all hides a capability that exists, and one with contradictory prices lies about it.
⚠️ EVERY ONE OF THESE IS SCOPED TO THIS STORE (`store_id`). `promotion.create` takes a nullable store,
and a promotion created without one is TENANT-WIDE — it would price the coffee shop and the Outlet too.
The platform's own bench runner (apps/api/scripts/seed-promotions.ts) omits it, which is right for the
single-store instance it was written for and wrong for this box's three.
_why_two_freights: ★ MEASURED 02/09, AND IT IS WHY THE ANNOUNCEMENT BAND ABOVE DERIVES ITS NUMBER. This store ends up with
TWO active free-shipping promotions, from two authors who never met:
· PROMO-06-FREE-SHIPPING-CAPPED — this list's own, from the dataset's pricing bench. Floor R$ 300,00,
and it covers AT MOST R$ 10,00 of the freight (`max_covered_amount: 1000`). Its own label is honest
about that — "Frete com desconto de até R$ 10,00" — and it carries `show_progress`, which is what
puts "faltam R$ X" in the cart.
· DEMO-HIST-01-FORGE — created by the KERNEL's own demo-data app when it seeds the dated past. Floor
R$ 299,00 and NO cap: this is the one that actually zeroes the freight.
⇒ A sentence written by looking at the first one would promise free shipping over R$ 300 and be false
for any freight above ten reais. The band therefore selects on the BENEFIT (uncapped, no method
restriction) rather than on a name, and takes the lowest floor among the ones that qualify.
⚠️ AND THE CAPPED ONE IS PROBABLY DEAD, WHICH IS AN OBSERVATION AND NOT A CHANGE. The engine orders two
comparable exclusive benefits by magnitude and an uncapped free shipping reaches infinity
(packages/core/src/promo/conflict.ts, `magnitudeOf`), so wherever the R$ 300 floor is met the R$ 299 one
is met too and wins. It is LEFT IN PLACE anyway: removing a name from this list does not delete the row
from a box that already has it, and `show_progress` is a capability the demo shows nowhere else.
Written down here rather than acted on — the decision of whether the pair survives is the merchant's.
